question_text: Do you like learning with friends? Please say why or why not.

evaluation_guide.expected_content: A short personal answer about whether the speaker likes learning with friends, with at least one simple reason.
evaluation_guide.key_points: Give a clear opinion; provide a simple reason, such as sharing ideas, feeling happier, or finding practice easier; use understandable pronunciation of common words.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Both yes and no answers are acceptable. The student may mention studying in class, doing homework together, or practicing speaking with classmates or friends.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Talking mainly about a favorite school subject without mentioning friends; describing a family member; discussing travel or expensive courses.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: Focus on intelligibility, stress, and basic sound production. Reward clear delivery even if the grammar is simple. A brief but direct answer can still be successful.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Speaking very quietly; unclear final sounds; leaving out important words; giving no reason; long pauses that make the message hard to follow.

suggested_ideas: how you feel when studying with friends
one good thing about learning with friends

question_text: Tell me about one activity you do when you learn with friends.

evaluation_guide.expected_content: A simple description of one learning activity the speaker does with friends.
evaluation_guide.key_points: Name one activity; give one or two details about how it happens; speak clearly enough for an average listener to understand.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Any common learning activity is acceptable, such as discussing lessons, practicing English, solving exercises together, or explaining ideas to each other.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Describing only a sports game with friends; listing many school rules; talking about a teacher instead of a shared activity.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: Listen for clear consonants and vowels in familiar words, natural word stress, and overall intelligibility. Minor grammar errors should not reduce the score if pronunciation is clear.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Speaking too fast and swallowing sounds; repeating the same word many times without adding detail; answering with only one word; unclear sentence endings.

question_text: Talk about learning with your friends. What do you learn together, and why do you like it?

evaluation_guide.expected_content: A short, simple description of learning with friends, including what they learn together and one reason the student likes it.
evaluation_guide.key_points: Name a subject, lesson, or activity; mention learning with friends; give one simple reason, such as saying it is fun or helpful.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: The student may talk about studying English, math, homework, reading, or practicing lessons with friends at school or after school. Simple present-tense answers are fine.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Talking only about playing with friends; talking only about a teacher; describing family study time instead of learning with friends.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: Prioritize clear pronunciation of common words in short connected speech. Listen for understandable key words and natural pausing. Do not over-penalize simple grammar mistakes.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Not mentioning friends; giving no clear learning activity; unclear pronunciation of key words; very long pauses before simple words.

suggested_ideas: why you like learning with friends
